title: Induction and non-Muslim expertise on the Singapore College of Islamic Studies committee
asked: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked what induction or onboarding plans exist for the Singapore College of Islamic Studies committee to understand the College's objectives, the community's aspirations and the student profile. She also asked what technical, professional and operational expertise non-Muslim committee members bring and how their roles support governance, institutional development and administrative effectiveness.
answered_by: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
response: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim said the Board of Governors and Steering Committee guide SCIS to nurture asatizah strong in Islamic knowledge and values who can help the community with contemporary challenges such as marriage, family and employment. Non-Muslim members make up less than half of the committees and are appointed for diverse expertise, including leading IHLs, social sciences, professional development, legal, financial and governance experience. All Board members undergo a structured induction programme covering the College's mission, vision, values and objectives, and engage with Muslim religious and community leaders, madrasah leaders and students, including at the 27 January SCIS symposium. Matters of faith and religious scholarship remain led by the Mufti, supported by the SCIS Advisory Panel and foreign Islamic institution partnerships.

key_points.point: The Board of Governors and Steering Committee guide SCIS to nurture future generations of asatizah.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: the Board of Governors and the Steering Committee of the Singapore College of Islamic Studies (SCIS) play important roles in developing and guiding SCIS to nurture future generations of asatizah

key_points.point: Asatizah are to be equipped with relevant skills such as the social sciences alongside Islamic studies.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: we must ensure that our asatizah are equipped with a range of relevant skills and knowledge, such as the social sciences, in addition to knowledge in Islamic studies

key_points.point: Non-Muslim members make up less than half of the Board of Governors and Steering Committee and are appointed for diverse expertise and experience with the Muslim community.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: The non-Muslim members make up less than half of the Board of Governors and Steering Committee, and are appointed for their diverse expertise and experience in working with the Muslim community.

key_points.point: These members include professionals and experts in leading IHLs, social sciences and professional development, contributing to SCIS' interdisciplinary approach.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: They include professionals and experts in areas such as leading Institutions of Higher Learning (IHLs), the social sciences and professional development, which contribute to SCIS' interdisciplinary approach.

key_points.point: Members with legal, financial and governance expertise support SCIS' corporate development and long-term sustainability.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Other members with legal, financial and governance expertise also support SCIS' corporate development and long-term sustainability.

key_points.point: Matters of faith and religious scholarship are led by the Mufti and supported by the SCIS Advisory Panel and foreign Islamic institution partnerships.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: Matters of faith and religious scholarship continue to be led by the Mufti and are supported by renowned Islamic scholars in the SCIS Advisory Panel as well as through partnerships with foreign Islamic institutions.

key_points.point: All Board members undergo a structured induction programme covering the College's mission, vision, values and objectives.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: All Board members undergo a structured induction programme, which includes briefings on the mission, vision and values, and objectives of the College.

key_points.point: Board members engage regularly with Muslim religious and community leaders, madrasah leaders and students.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: They also engage regularly with Muslim religious and community leaders as well as madrasah leaders and students to understand how the SCIS can best serve the community.

key_points.point: At the 27 January SCIS symposium, Board members interacted with madrasah students to understand their hopes and aspirations.
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
key_points.quote: at the recent SCIS symposium on 27 January, Board members had the opportunity to interact with madrasah students to understand their hopes and aspirations.

left_open: How the induction programme specifically caters to the profile of students.
How non-Muslim members' roles specifically support administrative effectiveness.
Whether the Steering Committee, as distinct from the Board of Governors, undergoes the same structured induction programme.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered succession planning, public participation, student intake and career pathways, and outreach and collaboration with other institutions.
